chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from Muhammad ibn Isa from Yahya ibn al-Hajjaj who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who said to me, 'Buy this garment and this animal specifically, and I will profit you by so-and-so much.' He said, 'There is no harm with that; buy it, and do not make the sale conditional before you have acquired ownership or purchased it.'

key_terms.تُوَاجِبْهُ: you make it conditional/make the sale contingent

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on buying goods with a guaranteed profit margin in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) validates a conditional sale where profit is promised, provided the condition of profit is not made a prerequisite for the validity of the sale contract itself (avoiding *bay' al-mu'allaq*). This ruling distinguishes between a valid sale with a stipulated outcome and a sale that is suspended or contingent upon that outcome, reflecting the Shia juristic emphasis on the independence of the contract from future uncertain events. It serves as a foundational text for understanding conditional transactions (*shurut*) in commercial jurisprudence.
